applies_why: The judge labels the Matthew 1:20 dispute UNDERDETERMINED while noting both the challenger's footed covenant-origin analogy and the sentence's own source statement, which is a verse-with-two-senses situation under K-S2.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand: (1) it applies when the sentence's own sense and a footed analogy both stand on the verse, so the matter is not open; (2) it applies only when one verse internally carries both senses, so separate analogical support can still leave UNDERDETERMINED.
why: The judge marks the matter UNDERDETERMINED although the text treats the verse as carrying both a footed covenant-origin sense and a source sense, and K-S2 says both senses stand rather than remain open.
